full_judgment: 6. Mr. Mohammad Nawab Ali, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the respondent, however, submitted That talaq as contemplated under Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 has made no distinction for various types of talaq recognized by Muslim Family Law including Khula and Mobaraka but speaks of pronouncement of talaq in any form whatsoever making a notice mandatory in writing of his having done so with a copy to the other partner so as to make it effective inasmuch as the Ordinance has not made any difference or distinction both the various types of talaq recognized by Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961. The learned Advocate-on-Record further submitted that in the present case the complainant-appellant herself admitted that no talaq took place and there is no further evidence at all on record to show that after pronouncement of talaq the respondent issued notice in writing upon the Chairman of the local Council informing the alleged fact of divorce or any copy of the said notice was ever sent to the respondent No.1 so as to make the talaq effective after expiry of 90 days upon delivery of the notice upon the Chairman of the local Council and in that view of the matter the marriage still subsists.
